nonce_lifecycle.advance_point: Immediately at allocation, not at successful commit. This is what makes an allocated seed consumed.
nonce_lifecycle.allocation: On an AUTO run, at the point the effective seed is derived and BEFORE any sampling: read the persisted auto_nonce, compute effective_seed = 48271^auto_nonce mod 2147483647, then persist auto_nonce + 1. Read-then-advance, in that order.
nonce_lifecycle.attempt_metadata: A failed AUTO attempt records the allocated effective_seed and the auto_nonce it consumed, alongside the failure. The prior successful result is untouched, but the failed allocation is visible - otherwise a consumed nonce would leave no trace and the sequence would appear to skip.
nonce_lifecycle.authority_vs_implementation: The AUTHORITY is effective_seed = 48271^auto_nonce mod 2147483647 - a modular power. A later VBA implementation must use an exact O(log nonce) modular exponentiation; O(nonce) repeated multiplication is not acceptable at large nonce and is not what the authority says. No implementation is proposed here.
nonce_lifecycle.auto_nonce_meaning: THE NEXT NONCE TO ALLOCATE. Not the last one used.
nonce_lifecycle.exhaustion: auto_nonce == 2147483646 must NOT be allocated: 48271^2147483646 == 1 == the seed for nonce 0, so allocating it silently reissues the first seed. Refuse the run.
nonce_lifecycle.failure_after_allocation: CONSUMES the nonce. The seed is spent even though the simulation failed, so a retry receives a NEW sequence rather than replaying the failed one. This is the inherited behaviour and it is a property of the ALLOCATION ORDER, which is why the order is stated above rather than left to the implementation.
nonce_lifecycle.failure_before_allocation: Consumes NO nonce. Nothing was allocated, so nothing is spent - a refusal on input validation leaves auto_nonce untouched.

primitive_root_test_uses: the DISTINCT prime divisors only - multiplicity is irrelevant to the test g^((p-1)/q) != 1, so the proof is unaffected by the earlier wording error
